patch.objective: Plan total knee arthroplasty rehab as the 2026 APTA guideline does: passive, active-assisted and active range of motion rather than continuous passive motion, progressive strengthening, and daily quadriceps NMES started early
secondaryObjectives: Recognizing red flags that require referral rather than continued PT management

sources.cite: APTA. Physical therapist management of total knee arthroplasty: revision 2026. Phys Ther. 2026;106. doi:10.1093/ptj/pzag058 (PMC13403188)
sources.note: Relayed from the DPT case tka-gait-dvt-red-flag, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 in the Europe PMC full text. Physical therapists should not use continuous passive motion after primary, uncomplicated TKA (high quality, strong); should include passive, active-assistive and active ROM exercise (moderate); should apply NMES to the quadriceps at least daily, started early, at the highest tolerable intensity (moderate). Team members should be aware of complications that may affect exercise, including thromboembolism.

sources.cite: Hillegass E, Puthoff M, Frese EM, et al. Role of physical therapists in the management of individuals at risk for or diagnosed with venous thromboembolism: evidence-based clinical practice guideline. Phys Ther. 2016;96:143-166
sources.note: Relayed from the DPT case tka-gait-dvt-red-flag, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (a hosted copy of the published PDF). Action statement 5: establish the likelihood of LE DVT when there is pain, tenderness, swelling, warmth or discoloration; action statement 6: recommend further medical testing after the Wells criteria, before mobilization; action statement 8: mobilize once anticoagulation has reached therapeutic levels. Wells (two-level): major surgery within 12 weeks, localized tenderness along the deep veins, entire leg swollen, calf swelling at least 3 cm more than the other side, pitting edema confined to the symptomatic leg and others score 1 each; an alternative diagnosis at least as likely scores -2; 2 or more is DVT likely, which calls for a duplex ultrasound before mobility.

sources.note: Relayed from the DPT case tka-gait-dvt-red-flag, not re-read for this band; its note: FLAG: read 2026-11-11 only through Guideline Central's pocket-guide summary (the publisher's full text could not be fetched): when signs and symptoms are present, determine the likelihood of VTE with standardized tools and share the results with the interprofessional team; mobilization begins once a medication's therapeutic level or an acceptable time after it has been reached; the risks of inactivity are greater than those of mobilization.

sources.cite: APTA Acute Care and APTA Cardiovascular and Pulmonary, Adult Vital Sign Interpretation in Acute Care Guide 2021 (boards approved March and April 2021)
sources.note: Relayed from the DPT case tka-gait-dvt-red-flag, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 through a text extraction of the PDF. Normal exercise response: HR rises about 10 beats/min per MET and returns to the pre-exercise level in 3-5 min; SBP rises about 10 mmHg per MET. Stop criteria include SBP drop >10 mmHg with increasing workload, new or worsening dysrhythmia, RR >40, unable to speak comfortably, SpO2 <90% or a drop of 4% or more (acute coronary syndrome), SpO2 <85% (lung disease); lung disease activity target 88-92%. Orthostatic hypotension: SBP drop >20 or DBP drop >10 mmHg within 3 min of standing. Beta blockers: lower HR with exercise and a dampened BP response; use the RPE scale in addition to HR.
